items.title: Melinda French Gates Doubles Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Donation Sum Bringing Total to $20 Million
items.summary:
Melinda French Gates has matched every dollar raised at Olivia Rodrigo's inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival, bringing the total headed to women-focused nonprofits to $20 million. Rodrigo announced the match from the stage at Great Park in Irvine on Saturday night, ahead of her headlining set, after telling a Friday press conference that the one-day event had raised $10 million.

Rodrigo framed the announcement around the artists who played the festival without pay. "The fact that they took the time out of their insanely busy schedules to come and do this festival for free is something I'm so grateful for," she said, before crediting ticket buyers for making the figure possible. She then introduced French Gates, who was in attendance, and revealed the pledge to double the day's total.

"Melinda is one of the most inspiring women I've ever met. She's devoted her life to empowering women and girls that might have otherwise been forgotten," Rodrigo said, according to The Hollywood Reporter. She added that she was "totally floored" by the match.

The $20 million will be split equally among 10 beneficiary organizations: Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, Center for Reproductive Rights, FreeFrom, Jhpiego, Johns Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health, National Women's Law Center and Planned Parenthood. Rodrigo said the groups are "doing incredibly important work every single day in the U.S. and globally," thanking every artist who waived a fee and every sponsor who signed on to an untested festival.

Rodrigo announced Daisy Chain Fields in June, and 2026 marked its first edition. Alongside her, the bill included Chappell Roan, Mitski, Doechii, Bikini Kill, the Breeders, Garbage, Eli, Quiet Light, Rachel Chinouriri, Devon Again and Not For Radio, with Stevie Nicks, Karen O and Lilith Fair founder Sarah McLachlan appearing as special guests. Katseye had been announced for the lineup but withdrew Thursday after member Megan sustained an injury.

items.title: See Kacey Musgraves Cover Dolly Parton’s ‘Here You Come Again’ in Boston
items.summary:
Kacey Musgraves devoted part of her Friday concert at TD Garden in Boston to Dolly Parton, who died Monday at 80. Musgraves brought back her Golden Hour ballad "Rainbow" — a song she had not played on her Middle of Nowhere Tour — and told the crowd that Parton had inspired it.

"Let's all sing this together for her memory," Musgraves said as images of Parton appeared on the screens behind her. She followed the ballad with a cover of "Here You Come Again," the 1977 single that carried Parton from country radio into pop.

The pairing of those two songs carried its own history. As Rolling Stone noted, Musgraves performed "Rainbow" at the 2019 Grammys before Parton and Katy Perry joined her for a group version of "Here You Come Again," and Musgraves and Perry sang the song again that same weekend at the MusiCares tribute to Parton.

Musgraves had already marked Parton's death on social media earlier in the week. "The world feels a lot less sparkly all of a sudden," she wrote. "Dolly. This really really hurts. So glad she's with her Carl Dean."

Musgraves remains out on the Middle of Nowhere Tour, where "Rainbow" had been absent from the setlist until Friday.

items.title: Olivia Rodrigo Recruits Alanis Morissette for a Surprise ‘Ironic’ Duet
items.summary:
Olivia Rodrigo covered a last-minute hole in her festival lineup by bringing out Alanis Morissette. At the inaugural Daisy Chain Fields on Saturday, Aug. 29, at Great Park in Irvine, Calif., Rodrigo told the crowd that Yeah Yeah Yeahs frontwoman Karen O had withdrawn from the all-women bill, then introduced Morissette in her place.

Rodrigo broke the news herself before the substitution. "The bad news is Karen O is not able to make it tonight, she was one of the first people who said yes to Daisy Chain but she has a personal matter that requires her to be elsewhere," she said. Morissette walked out shortly after, and the two performed "Ironic," the single from her 1995 album Jagged Little Pill, flipping the song's much-quoted "beautiful wife" line to a "beautiful husband" partway through.

The duet had a long runway. Rodrigo has repeatedly cited Jagged Little Pill as foundational to her songwriting, inducted Morissette into the Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2022, and sang "You Oughta Know" with her during a Los Angeles stop on the Sour tour.

Rodrigo staged the festival from a commercial peak. As Billboard reported, her third album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, entered the Billboard 200 at No. 1 in June with 485,000 equivalent album units, the biggest week of her career and the largest of 2026 for any solo artist. Lead single "drop dead" debuted atop the Hot 100, her fourth No. 1 debut, making her the second artist after Beyoncé to send each of her first three albums to No. 1 while pulling a Hot 100 leader from each.

The one-day event raised $10 million for nonprofits supporting women and girls, and its bill also included Chappell Roan and Doechii. Rodrigo begins her Unraveled Tour in a matter of weeks.

items.title: Harry Styles Pokes Fun at Ex Taylor Swift’s Wedding During Madison Square Garden Show
items.summary:
Harry Styles opened his 30-night residency at Madison Square Garden on Saturday, and closed the show with a joke about Taylor Swift's wedding to Travis Kelce, which took place at the same arena. "We're at Madison Square Garden, home of the world champion New York Knicks!" Styles told the crowd, then added, "And they also do weddings."

Earlier in the evening, Styles paid tribute to Dolly Parton, who died this week. The Swift line came at the tail end of the set.

Styles and Swift dated from November 2012 to January 2013, and he is widely understood to be the subject of her 2014 single "Style." Variety reported that Styles was invited to the July 3 wedding to the NFL star at Madison Square Garden but could not attend because of his tour schedule; his fiancée, Zoë Kravitz, went in his place.

The two exes have kept things cordial. On July 3, during his Wembley residency, Styles performed "Two Ghosts," the 2017 song long read as his reply to "Style," with its lines about the "same lips red, same eyes blue / Same white shirt, couple more tattoos."

Styles has 29 more nights booked at the Garden.

items.title: In Latest Threat Of Regulatory Retaliation, Donald Trump Says He’ll Report NBC News’ Kristen Welker To FCC For “Rebuke Or Punishment”
items.summary:
Donald Trump said Sunday that he will report NBC News' Kristen Welker to the Federal Communications Commission for "rebuke or punishment," objecting to her characterization of his record endorsing political candidates. The threat lands while the FCC is already defending itself against an ABC lawsuit alleging that its regulatory actions amount to retaliation over news coverage.

Welker's comment came not on Meet the Press but during an appearance on Washington, D.C., affiliate WRC-TV. Discussing the midterms, she said Trump "has endorsed a slate of candidates in the primaries" and "has had some mixed results," while noting that his pick of Senator Darline Graham had prevailed in South Carolina and now faces Dr. Annie Andrews.

Trump disputed the framing on Truth Social, calling the show "Meet the Fake Press" and asserting a 100% record on Senate endorsements and 98% on House races. "How can anyone be allowed to say this, working for freely given Public Airwaves?" he wrote, adding, "Because of this purposeful inaccuracy, she will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment." A second post read, "THE FAKE POLLS USED BY OUR CROOKED MEDIA ARE OUT OF CONTROL, AND SOMETHING MUST BE DONE ABOUT IT. FCC TO THE RESCUE!"

Deadline noted that several Trump-endorsed candidates have lost recent races, including Mike Lindell in the Minnesota governor's primary, Rep. Andy Ogles in Tennessee, Rep. Randy Feenstra in Iowa's governor's primary and Burt Jones in Georgia's.

ABC sued the FCC this month on First Amendment grounds, citing Trump's Truth Social threats as evidence and challenging Chairman Brendan Carr's order that the network's eight owned stations submit their broadcast licenses for early renewal. The FCC responded that "all broadcasters have a legal obligation to operate in the public interest — even Disney," and pointed to a year-long examination of DEI discrimination claims. A judge will hear the network's request for a temporary restraining order in October.

The FCC's own guidance limits its news distortion authority to reports deliberately intended to mislead, and states that it does not investigate "claims of collateral inaccuracy in news reports or differences of opinion." NBC News has not commented, and an FCC spokesperson did not immediately respond to Deadline's request.
